source.author: verg
source.text: Sed pater omnipotens speluncis abdidit atris, hoc metuens, molemque et montis insuper altos imposuit, regemque dedit, qui foedere certo et premere et laxas sciret dare iussus habenas.
source.text_original: Sed pater omnipotens speluncis abdidit atris, / hoc metuens, molemque et montis insuper altos / imposuit, regemque dedit, qui foedere certo / et premere et laxas sciret dare iussus habenas.
source.text_english: But the all-powerful father hid her in dark caverns, fearing this, and placed over her the mass and the high mountains, and he appointed a king who, by a fixed covenant, should know both how to press down and, when ordered, to let loose the slack reins.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hoc metuens et nequa foret manus invida nato, non mediae telluris opes, non improba legi divitis arva plagae teneant uberrima Teucer et Libys et vestri Pelopis domus: horrida saevo quae premis arva gelu strictosque insedimus amnes.
reuse.text_original: hoc metuens et nequa foret manus invida nato, / non mediae telluris opes, non improba legi / divitis arva plagae (teneant uberrima Teucer / et Libys et vestri Pelopis domus): horrida saevo / quae premis arva gelu strictosque insedimus amnes.
reuse.text_english: Fearing this, and lest the hand of envy should be ill-disposed toward his son, let not the wealth of the middle land, let not the rich fields of the unruly tract, most fertile Teucer and Libys and the house of your Pelops, hold him fast: the rough fields that you press with cruel frost and the frozen rivers we have settled on.
